name: mighty-max
description: MiniMax M-series language models for VS Code Chat (BYOK)

mightymax-head.description: Mighty Max aviator glyph (used as the status-bar item icon).

commands.title: Mighty Max: Manage MCP Reserved Tools

apiKey.description: MiniMax API key. Stored in SecretStorage by the `Mighty Max: Manage MiniMax` command. Required for the model picker to surface this vendor.

mightyMax.baseUrl.description: MiniMax API base URL. The API key is never stored here — it lives in SecretStorage.

mightyMax.firstByteTimeoutMs.description: Watchdog on time-to-first-response, in milliseconds. If MiniMax accepts the connection but sends no response headers within this budget, the attempt is aborted and retried with backoff; exhausted retries surface a 'stall' error instead of hanging until you cancel. Healthy requests return headers in single-digit seconds even on large cached prompts. Changes apply to the next request — no reload needed.

mightyMax.idleTimeoutMs.description: Watchdog on mid-stream silence, in milliseconds. If an open response stream delivers no bytes for this long, it is cut with a 'stall' error (and retried automatically when nothing had streamed yet). This measures gaps between bytes, not total request time — long responses that keep streaming are never cut. Changes apply to the next request — no reload needed.

mightyMax.logLevel.description: Log level for Mighty Max. Logs never contain the API key, Authorization header, or request/response bodies.

mightyMax.enableSmartToolFiltering.description: Smart tool filtering. When enabled, the agent's tool set is capped at `mightyMax.maxTools` (default 60) for built-in tools, with MCP tools governed separately by a rolling LRU — see `mightyMax.mcpMaxTools` (default 60). History-referenced tools and the always-on pin list (`copilot_*`, `run_in_terminal`, `apply_patch`, `grep_search`, `file_search`, `semantic_search`) always survive the cap. The full VS Code tool set is ~83 entries on a typical install; with several MCP servers installed the total can climb into the hundreds — keeping the wire payload small directly reduces first-turn latency on MiniMax M3 (Anthropic endpoint) where tool-schema size dominates the cold-cache build. Set to `false` to forward every tool verbatim; the pin list, MCP LRU, and history-referenced set are still honored.

mightyMax.maxTools.description: Maximum number of built-in (non-MCP) tools to send to the model when smart filtering is enabled. M3 handles 60 cleanly; Copilot Chat's virtual-tool grouper handles larger sets at the chat-UI level, not here. MCP tools are governed separately by a rolling LRU; see `mightyMax.mcpMaxTools`.

mightyMax.mcpMaxTools.description: Maximum number of MCP tools to keep in the wire payload on any given request. Distinct from `mightyMax.maxTools` (which caps built-ins). The chat-provider maintains a per-tool recency tracker: tools the model has called stay in the wire permanently for the session; new tools displace unused ones on a recency-ordered first-in basis. Setting to 0 disables MCP tool inclusion entirely; the model can still see MCP servers via the live tool set on the chat UI side. Reserved entries from `mightyMax.reservedMcpTools` count against this cap.

mightyMax.reservedMcpTools.description: MCP tools (or prefixes ending in `_`) to keep in the wire payload on every request, regardless of recency. Each entry costs one slot of the `mightyMax.mcpMaxTools` cap. The platform's built-in agent tools (`copilot_*`, `run_in_terminal`, `apply_patch`, `grep_search`, `file_search`, `semantic_search`) are always-included separately and cannot be removed. The chat-provider warns at request time if the reserved list length exceeds the cap. The shipped default (`mcp_github_`) is a broad prefix that pins every tool any GitHub MCP server exposes — the official `github-mcp-server`, community variants, and forks all land in the `mcp_github_<...>` namespace, so a single entry covers them all. Add more entries for additional servers the model needs available on every turn; leave the default list in place to let the rolling LRU handle MCP selection on recency alone for the rest.

mightyMax.alwaysIncludeTools.description: Tools to keep regardless of relevance scoring when filtering is enabled. Supports exact names (run_in_terminal), prefix pins (copilot_ matches every copilot_* built-in), and substring matches (grep matches grep_search, grep_file_contents). Tools referenced by the current request's tool_use/tool_result history are also pinned automatically. MCP tools are governed separately by the rolling LRU — see `mightyMax.mcpMaxTools`.

enumDescriptions: Filter based on semantic relevance to the current prompt (keyword matching)
Filter based on historical usage patterns (frequently-used tools prioritized)
Combine relevance and usage scoring for balanced filtering
mightyMax.toolFilterStrategy.description: Strategy for selecting which tools to include when filtering is enabled.

mightyMax.systemPrompt.description: Optional system prompt sent on every M3 request. When empty, Mighty Max uses a short preamble that nudges M3 to plan before the first tool call. The prompt is sanitized for UTF-16 surrogate code points and sent with `cache_control: ephemeral` so it is reused across requests.

mightyMax.enableNativeTokenCounting.description: Use MiniMax M3's native Anthropic-compatible token-count endpoint for Copilot Chat context estimates. Requests are short-lived cached and automatically fall back to a local heuristic if the endpoint is unavailable.

enumDescriptions: Enable MiniMax M3 adaptive thinking for stronger planning and interleaved tool use.
Disable visible MiniMax M3 thinking for lower-latency, direct responses.
mightyMax.m3ThinkingMode.description: Controls MiniMax M3 thinking on the Anthropic-compatible endpoint. M2-family models retain their native reasoning behavior.

mightyMax.toolResultMaxChars.description: Maximum characters retained for each tool result sent back to MiniMax. Larger values preserve more terminal/search output but consume more context and may increase latency.

mightyMax.enableAutoKeyRotation.description: When enabled, if the active MiniMax API key is rejected by the API (401/403), Mighty Max transparently retries the request with the next healthy stored key. When disabled, the auth error surfaces to chat immediately and you must change keys manually via 'Mighty Max: Manage' (or the 'Manage API keys' submenu). Auto-rotation only matters when multiple keys are stored — with a single stored key the behavior is the same either way. Flip this setting in-app via 'Mighty Max: Manage' → 'Toggle auto-rotation' (the row label shows the current state: '● … ON' / '○ … OFF').
